svg.title: Thermal programming of phase assemblage, dissolution, interfacial pH and cytocompatibility in Ca–Si–P–O glass-ceramics (700 vs 1100 °C)
svg.desc: Four panels. A: phase composition (wt%) and bulk density versus sintering temperature. B: cumulative mass loss versus immersion time with Korsmeyer–Peppas fits. C: interfacial pH versus time with the physiological window shaded. D: cell viability versus extract concentration with the ISO 10993-5 70% threshold.
svg.text: Thermal Programming of Phase Architecture and Ion Release
Ca–Si–P–O bioactive glass-ceramics · 700 °C vs 1100 °C processing · phase assemblage → dissolution → interfacial pH → cytocompatibility
700 °C peaks at pH 8.55 (3 d); 1100 °C stays within the window
1100 °C ≥ 190% viability at every dose; 700 °C falls below 70% at ≥ 80% extract
Ca : Si ≈ 3.0 at both temperatures · ≈ 4× higher release at 700 °C
